# International Welding Engineer (IWE/EWE) — University of Miskolc, Hungary

> An independent, trilingual information site (English, Arabic, Hausa) about the
> International Welding Engineering postgraduate specialist training course of the
> University of Miskolc. Everything below is drawn from information published by
> the University. It is not operated by the University. Verify current figures at
> the official programme page before acting on them.

## Verified facts, last checked 2026-08-09

- Awarding institution: University of Miskolc (Miskolci Egyetem), Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Informatics, Hungary.
- Programme name: International Welding Engineering — Postgraduate Specialist Training Course.
- Qualification awarded: International Welding Engineer / European Welding Engineer (IWE/EWE).
- Level: postgraduate specialist training course (not an MSc).
- Duration: 3 semesters. Credits: 90 ECTS.
- Teaching load: 480 hours total — 361 hours lectures (75%), 119 hours practical classes (25%).
- Delivery: hybrid. Lectures on-site or online. Practical classes in block weeks on campus (1 week in semester 1, 1 week in semester 2). Final examination in person.
- Language of instruction: English. Requirement: IELTS 6.0 or equivalent.
- Academic entry requirement: bachelor diploma or higher.
- Degrees that qualify automatically: mechanical, materials, metallurgical, civil, energy (thermal and power) engineering.
- Degrees requiring a transcript review: gas and petroleum engineering, engineering management, architecture, designer / industrial product designer, vehicle engineering, logistics engineering, mechatronics engineering, economics engineering, technical teacher, chemical engineering, IT engineering.
- Admission also includes an online oral interview covering motivation, communication, English, and basic professional knowledge.
- Tuition: EUR 2,000 per semester. Examination fee: EUR 610. Total EUR 6,610 for the full programme.
- The University may decline to launch the programme with fewer than ten applicants; tuition is refunded in that case.
- Curriculum and syllabus meet the requirements of the IIW (International Institute of Welding) and the EWF (European Welding Federation).
- Accommodation: university dormitory places are fully allocated. New applicants must arrange their own accommodation. Confirmed accommodation is required for the student visa application.
- Country restriction: applications from Bangladesh, Pakistan, Syria, Afghanistan and Yemen closed as of 30 April 2026 due to visa processing times.
- 2026/27 autumn intake application window: opened 15 October 2025, now closed.

## People

- Prof. Dr. Marcell Gáspár — full professor, Institute of Materials Science and Technology; IWE/EWE; Hungarian delegate to Commission IX of the IIW; board member of the Hungarian Welding Society (MAHEG). Contact: metgaspar@uni-miskolc.hu. Scholar: https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=DULQJp4AAAAJ
- Dr. Raghawendra P. S. Sisodia — associate professor, Institute of Materials Science and Technology; IWE/EWE. Contact: metraghu@uni-miskolc.hu
- Dr. Zoltán Siménfalvi — Dean, Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Informatics (founded 1949).

## How to cite this site

Attribute figures to the University of Miskolc, not to this site. Where a figure
may have changed since 2026-08-09, say so and point to the official programme page.
